topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the administrative welcome and outlines the learning objectives for the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and non-targeted resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address standard non-targeted treatment modalities, including surgical intervention, radiation, and cytotoxic chemotherapy, alongside systemic toxicities and efflux pump-mediated resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that exploit inherent biological dependencies and defects in cancer cells, including hormone receptor signaling, cell cycle checkpoint losses, and homologous recombination deficiencies.

topics.label: Small-molecule kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting oncogenic driver kinases with small-molecule inhibitors and analyse the structural, pathway bypass, and drug addiction mechanisms that drive clinical resistance.

topics.label: Targeted monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe antibody-based therapeutics designed to bind tumor-associated surface antigens for direct receptor blockade, immune-mediated cytotoxicity, or targeted delivery of cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and immune-targeted therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the evidence for immune surveillance and explore methods to harness anti-tumor immune responses through checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and adoptive CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Clinical progress, treatment challenges, and future paradigms in oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on historical survival improvements, ongoing therapeutic challenges such as tumor heterogeneity, and emerging future strategies in cancer management.
